## Lateral face covariance and centroid correction (`SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE`) {#sec-ch12-flux-covariance}

<!-- PROVENANCE

Local symbols (pending notation integration): $\sigma^{2,\mathrm{face}}_i$ is the x1 variance
on the lateral face measure in $\mathrm{m^2}$; $\delta^{\mathrm{face}}_i$ is the cell centroid minus
that face's radial centroid in $\mathrm m$. These are distinct from the cell variance $\sigma_i^2$
and the cell-minus-midpoint offset $\delta_i$.

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
Default: **off**. Enable with `SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE=1`. The x2/x3 correction has both a covariance term and a cell-to-face centroid
term. Each direction's geometric pressure source is corrected only if that direction's flux correction exists.
It is a leading smooth-gradient correction, not a fourth-order solver switch.
:::

### Derivation

Expand two smooth fields about the cell centroid. The average of their linear product is the product of their
averages plus $\sigma_i^2\partial_1a\partial_1b$, where $\sigma_i^2$ is the second central moment in $\mathrm{m^2}$.
For density-weighted primitives, expansion of the ratios cancels the density-gradient pairs: a transported scalar
has leading covariance $\sigma_i^2\rho\partial_1v_a\partial_1q$. Total mass is linear in stored momentum,
so its covariance is zero. Species covariance is subtracted from dry mass, preserving their total.
A face has its own centroid; shifting from the cell centroid adds
$-\delta^{\mathrm{face}}_i\partial_1\mathbf F_a$ to the advective flux being corrected. Thus the implemented enthalpy correction has two pieces:

$$
(\Delta\mathbf F_a)_E=
\sigma^{2,\mathrm{face}}_i\rho\,\partial_1\!\left(\frac{\rho e+p}{\rho}\right)\partial_1v_a
-\delta^{\mathrm{face}}_i\partial_1\!\left[(\rho e+p)v_a\right],\qquad a\in\{2,3\}.
$$ {#eq-ch12-flux-covariance-energy}

Here $e$ is specific internal energy in $\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}}$ and $v_a$ is the face-local normal speed in
$\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The subscript $E$ selects the energy row of the flux vector; the correction shown uses enthalpy, excluding kinetic energy.
The flux density has units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$.
`_flux_covariance` implements @eq-ch12-flux-covariance-energy ([`hydro_forward.cpp:54-191`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L54-L191)); the face variance is used in this
formula, rather than substituting the cell variance on curved grids. Adding the term to a shared face flux makes
its two neighboring volume-integrated increments cancel. This telescoping is exact; dropping horizontal-gradient
products, velocity-squared covariance and the pressure Hessian is a truncation assumption.
`configuration_check.py` checks the linear covariance identity and two-cell telescoping.
Source derivation: `docs/derivations/289-covariance-x3-curved.md@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0` §2A and 4B.

### Numerical method

At each hydro call, average the reconstructed left/right primitives, project a copy into the face-local frame,
and difference along x1. Fewer than three x1 entries or shallow water returns no correction. Add the correction
to each active lateral face flux. The corresponding geometric source uses pressure reduced by the centroid shift
times its x1 derivative, while an inactive direction retains ordinary pressure. No separate MPI synchronization
is introduced by this switch.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
No new order fit is supplied. Curved-grid centroid terms do not vanish for an isothermal moving state; exact rest
requires zero velocity. MPI-rank seams and XC+FC are unmeasured here.

The complete switch inventory is @sec-ch12-matrix.
:::
